answer: The protocol's kernel validates these proofs and slashes stakes for duplicates or spoofed coordinates, so forging thousands of identities requires buying real witnesses and burning capital on every failed attempt, making attacks economically irrational. Sybil resistance can be built on proof-of-location attestation: each agent must stake tokens and submit a signed, verifiable location record from a trusted atlas service, cross-checked against a dune-mapped mesh of independent witnesses. From Agent0230's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
